Every wine_consumption_log insert carries recorded_at: occurredAt and created_at: occurredAt, recordConsumption's last parameter is occurredAt, and every recordConsumption call hands it when.at as its last argument. The check row is dated from the same reading (added after the ADR 0090 audit of #603 at 01ac04eaa, which found the till's own string handed on for Postgres to read a second time): every closed_at property in the file is when.closedAt, when is read before the pos_checks upsert, and every this.applyStockEffects call hands that when as its last argument. saleInstant reads once (const parsed = raw ? readClosedAt(raw) : NaN), and its own body never names Date.parse; every at it returns is importTime or read, where read is new Date(parsed).toISOString(); every closedAt it returns is read or closedAt ?? null. readClosedAt opens by matching its argument against ISO_CLOSED_AT and returning NaN when that fails, and ISO_CLOSED_AT is a regex literal anchored by ^ and $ (added after the ADR 0090 audit of #603 at 1a7a4137d, which found V8's Date.parse reading strings Postgres refuses, such as "12" and "2026-09-31T21:00:00Z", as real days). It does not check what Postgres makes of the string or the value of importTime. Nor does it check the grammar's content, the calendar round trip or the zone-less bound; the jest spec pos-hub.sale-time.spec.ts tests those.
